title: Multi‑Currency Procurement and Revenue Recognition Guidance for Contract Triggers
author: Elena Martinez
content:
Summary:

This guidance establishes standard handling for procurement and B2B contract scenarios where (a) customer pricing, billing or acceptance is denominated in a foreign currency, and (b) contract terms create non-standard revenue recognition triggers (e.g., milestone-based billing, usage thresholds invoiced retrospectively, or capacity commitments with true-ups). The goal is to reduce month-end reconciliation risk, ensure consistent accounting treatment, and provide procurement and legal teams with boilerplate clauses and an approval checklist.

Scope:
- Applies to all commercial contracts that include: multi-currency settlements, milestone/thresholded billing, capacity commits with true-ups, or deferred invoicing longer than 30 days.
- Does NOT replace detailed ASC 606 or IFRS 15 assessments for complex, bespoke contracts; it provides operational standards and routing for accounting review.

Key definitions:
- Transaction Currency: currency in which the contract states prices and invoices are issued.
- Functional Currency: Redwood's reporting currency (USD).
- FX Revaluation Date: the date we remeasure contract assets/liabilities per accounting policy (monthly close).
- Recognition Trigger: a contractual event that creates the right to consideration or the satisfied performance obligation (e.g., delivery, acceptance, usage threshold reached).

Policy overview:
1) Price and Invoice Currency:
- Wherever possible, contracts should price and invoice in USD. If customer insists on local currency, Legal must include an explicit FX clause (see Clauses to Include section).
- Procurement must capture the Transaction Currency in the procurement system (Coupa/NetSuite field: transaction_currency).

2) Contract-level Accounting Assessment:
- All multi-currency or milestone contracts are routed to Accounting (revrec@redwood.com) during contracting. Accounting will confirm: allocation of transaction price, identification of performance obligations, and expected timing of recognition.

3) FX treatment and monthly close:
- Monetary items (receivables/payables) are remeasured at the FX spot rate on the balance sheet date.
- Non-monetary contract balances (unearned revenue measured on a unit-of-account basis) are translated at the rate at inception unless the contract requires later adjustment.

Procedures (contract drafting and pre-execution):
1) Procurement checklist before signature (must be attached to Procurement ticket):
   1.1 Confirm Transaction Currency field populated and indicate if hedging is requested.
   1.2 Confirm billing cadence (monthly/quarterly/milestone/usage-based) and define how usage is measured.
   1.3 If milestones or acceptance events are present, add clear, objective acceptance criteria and date-based fallback.
   1.4 For multi-currency deals, include FX clause template (below) and indicate whether customer or Redwood bears FX variance.
   1.5 Attach expected schedule of recognition and draft journal entry examples for Accounting review.
   1.6 Obtain Sign‑off: Legal, Sales Finance, and Accounting (email or e-signature).

2) Live contract amendments and true-ups:
- If a customer executes a true-up (e.g., exceeded committed tokens/GPU hours), the invoice currency and recognition follow the original contract unless an amendment states otherwise. Record true-up as additional consideration; allocate to existing performance obligations per ASC 606 rules.

Accounting treatment — common scenarios and sample entries (USD functional currency):

Scenario A: Customer billed in EUR for monthly subscription, billed in arrears on the 5th of each month.
- Recognition: revenue recognized ratably over the month as performance obligation is satisfied.
- Close treatment (example for a January invoice of EUR 50,000, FX spot on Jan 31 = 1.10 USD/EUR):
  - When invoice issued on Feb 05 (EUR 50,000): 
    - Accounts Receivable (EUR 50,000) recorded at the invoice date spot if using transactional approach.
    - For month-end Jan 31, if services performed in January but invoice not yet issued, record contract asset (unbilled receivable) in USD using average or spot guidance per accounting policy.
  - Sample closing journal (simplified):
    - Jan 31 (to accrue earned revenue): Dr Contract Asset (USD) 55,000; Cr Revenue 55,000.
    - Feb 05 (when invoice issued): Dr Accounts Receivable (EUR 50,000) / Cr Contract Asset (USD 55,000) and recognize FX difference in Other Income/FX Loss.

Scenario B: Milestone payment in JPY with acceptance clause and 30-day invoice terms.
- Ensure acceptance criteria include a fallback acceptance-by-date clause to avoid recognition delay.
- Sample clause (legal template below).

Journal entry examples (illustrative):
- When milestone achieved but invoice in foreign currency and not yet billed (accrual):
  - Dr Contract Asset (USD) X; Cr Revenue (USD) X
- When invoice issued in foreign currency and recorded:
  - Dr Accounts Receivable (JPY Y); Cr Contract Asset (USD X)
  - On settlement: Dr Cash (USD) Z; Cr Accounts Receivable (JPY Y) and record FX remeasurement to clear AR.

Contract clauses to include (templates):
1) FX clause — two options (select one):
- Option A (customer bears FX risk): "All prices and invoices denominated in [Transaction Currency]. Customer is responsible for any FX differences arising between invoice date and payment date; Redwood will invoice in [Transaction Currency]."
- Option B (Redwood bears FX risk): "All prices are set in USD and amounts billed in [Local Currency] are for convenience only. Payments received in Local Currency will be converted to USD at Redwood's spot rate on the date of receipt for accounting purposes."

2) Acceptance fallback clause (to avoid open-ended recognition delays):
"If the Customer does not provide written acceptance or documented rejection within 15 business days following delivery, the deliverable shall be deemed accepted on the 16th business day and any related milestone shall be deemed satisfied for invoicing and revenue recognition purposes."

3) Billing & True-up clause:
"Usage true-ups will be invoiced monthly in arrears. The Parties agree that invoices are due within 30 days. Any disputes to amounts must be raised within 30 days of invoice receipt; undisputed amounts remain due and payable."

Approval matrix (thresholds are USD equivalent):
| Contract Value | Required Approvals | Additional Steps |
|---------------:|-------------------|------------------|
| < 50,000       | Procurement Owner; Line Manager | Standard procurement review |
| 50,000 - 500,000 | Procurement Owner; Sales Finance; Legal | Accounting pre-signoff required |
| > 500,000      | Head of Finance; Legal; CRO | RevRec detailed assessment; Board notification for multi-year >2yr |

Escalation flow for close exceptions (month-end differences >USD 10k):
1) Finance Ops raises an exception ticket and routes to Sales Finance and Procurement.
2) If unresolved in 48 hours, alert Head of Revenue Operations and schedule an ad-hoc reconciliation call.
3) If legal interpretation needed (e.g., disputed acceptance), tag Legal and schedule decision within 5 business days.

Operational considerations and system fields (minimum required):
- Procurement system: transaction_currency, fx_hedge_requested (Y/N), billing_cadence, revenue_account_code, revrec_trigger (deliverable/milestone/usage), base_price_local and base_price_usd_estimate.
- Accounting system (NetSuite): contract_reference, deferred_revenue_schedule_id, realized_fx_gain_loss_account.

Reporting and dashboards:
- Monthly: a multi-currency close dashboard showing open AR by currency, unbilled contract assets, FX unrealized gain/loss, and invoices >60 days overdue. Owner: Finance Ops.
- Quarterly: summary of revenue recognized in non-USD currencies and P&L FX impact. Owner: FP&A.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ):
Q: Who chooses whether to hedge currency exposure?
A: Treasury/FP&A evaluates hedging for exposures >USD 250k expected over the next 90 days. Procurement indicates hedge request on the procurement ticket.

Q: If a contract is amended to change currency mid-term, what happens?
A: Amendments that change Transaction Currency require Accounting reassessment. Prior balances remain in original currency; future invoicing follows the amended currency.
